original_question: For a given field F, which finite groups G are F-admissible, meaning that there exists a G-crossed-product F-division algebra?
target_in_paper: Section 11.A, Problem 11.1: determine which groups are F-admissible, for a field F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s intended target almost verbatim: fix a field F, restrict to finite groups G, and ask which G are F-admissible, meaning that there exists a G-crossed-product F-division algebra. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
missing_details: An F-division algebra in this paper is implicitly finite-dimensional, central, and simple over F, with no nontrivial one-sided ideals; in particular, its center is exactly F. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

The background definition of crossed product is being used: a central simple F-algebra B is a crossed product if it contains a maximal torus that is Galois over F. That is the hidden structure behind the phrase G-crossed product. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

For a division algebra, this crossed-product condition specializes to the familiar maximal-subfield formulation; this is a direct division-algebra specialization of the background definitions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

The official target is the general fixed-field classification problem, not the narrower neighboring Q-admissibility conjecture asking whether every Sylow-metacyclic group is Q-admissible. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

The nearby context notes that the problem extends the inverse Galois problem and is especially interesting when F = Q; that motivation is absent from the draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a field F. Determine all finite groups G for which there exists a finite-dimensional central division F-algebra A that is a G-crossed product over F; concretely, in the division-algebra setting, this asks for A to contain a maximal subfield L such that L/F is Galois with Gal(L/F) ≅ G. In other words, classify the F-admissible finite groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s own statement, so the correct target is Problem 11.1 in §11.A rather than the neighboring Problem 11.2. I only made explicit the background assumptions that the algebra is central over F and finite-dimensional, and I unpacked crossed product using the paper’s definition. I did not specialize to F = Q or add a Sylow-metacyclic hypothesis, because those belong to the special Q-admissibility conjecture and to the subsequent number-field discussion, not to the official formulation of Problem 11.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
